what_is_open: A sharp minimax mean-squared-error rate over a precisely defined shrinking-separation triangular class, a data-driven selector attaining that rate across ordinary DML, finite-order ACE, and global-contour regimes, a specified uniformly valid confidence procedure, and a matching local minimax lower bound remain undetermined.
obstruction: The current node explicitly defines a research agenda rather than a formal existence claim: neither a unique sharp-rate functional nor a uniform-inference/coverage criterion is defined. Its frozen dependencies establish a matched fixed-separation rate and two shrinking-separation upper benchmarks, but they supply no selector, confidence procedure, or full-class local converse from which the requested joint conclusion could be derived.
attempted: The ordinary-DML and local-ACE guarantees can be combined only into a pointwise oracle minimum, which is not a data-driven rule. The fixed-separation contour argument is not uniform as the separation vanishes because its localization radius, contour certificate, and risk constant depend on the fixed separation. The Gaussian--Rademacher calculation supplies only a path-specific upper bound and therefore cannot certify a full-class minimax rate or matching lower bound.
partial_result:
At every fixed \(\delta>0\), \(\text{thm:adaptive-rootn-minimax}\) gives a total ordinary-sample Borel statistic satisfying
\[
 \frac{c}{n}\le \mathfrak R_n^{\mathrm{NG}}\le \frac{C}{n}
\]
whenever \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\varepsilon_0\); the executable represented-data conclusion is conditional on implementing and compiling \(\text{def:certified-contour-arithmetic-substrate}\). Along \(\delta_n\downarrow0\), \(\text{thm:local-to-gaussian-partial-benchmarks}\) proves the explicit local ACE generalized-quantile upper benchmark proportional to \(\delta_n^{-1}\) under its displayed eligibility condition. On the Gaussian--Rademacher path with \(\Delta_a=2a^4\), it also proves
\[
 \sup_P E_P\!\left[(\widehat\theta_{a,n}-\theta_0(P))^2\right]
 \le C\min\!\left\{1,
 n^{-1}\Delta_a^{-1/2}
 \exp\!\left(\frac{\pi^2\sqrt2}{4}\Delta_a^{-1/2}\right)
 \right\}
\]
provided \(\varepsilon_{1,n}\le\Delta_a^{1/4}/(2^{1/4}\pi)\). These results do not define or attain a sharp full-class shrinking-separation rate, construct an adaptive selector or confidence procedure, or furnish a matching local lower bound.
